+    CONST("frame", "send one frame for each frame", 0, "mode"),
+    CONST("field", "send one frame for each field", 1, "mode"),
+    { "parity", "specify the assumed picture field parity", OFFSET(parity), AV_OPT_TYPE_INT, {.i64=-1}, -1, 1, FLAGS, "parity" },
+    CONST("tff",  "assume top field first",    0, "parity"),
+    CONST("bff",  "assume bottom field first", 1, "parity"),
+    CONST("auto", "auto detect parity",       -1, "parity"),
+    { "deint",  "specify which frames to deinterlace", OFFSET(deint), AV_OPT_TYPE_INT, {.i64=0}, 0, 1, FLAGS, "deint" },
+    CONST("all",        "deinterlace all frames",                       0, "deint"),
+    CONST("interlaced", "only deinterlace frames marked as interlaced", 1, "deint"),
+    { "rslope", "specify the search radius for edge slope tracing", OFFSET(rslope), AV_OPT_TYPE_INT, {.i64=1}, 1, MAX_R, FLAGS, },
+    { "redge",  "specify the search radius for best edge matching", OFFSET(redge),  AV_OPT_TYPE_INT, {.i64=2}, 0, MAX_R, FLAGS, },
+    { NULL }
+};
+
+AVFILTER_DEFINE_CLASS(estdif);
+
+static int query_formats(AVFilterContext *ctx)
+{
+    static const enum AVPixelFormat pix_fmts[] = {
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUV410P, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV411P,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUV420P, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV422P,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUV440P, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV444P,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUVJ444P, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVJ440P,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUVJ422P, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVJ420P,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUVJ411P,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA420P, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA422P, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA444P,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_GBRP, AV_PIX_FMT_GBRAP,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_GRAY8,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_GRAY9, AV_PIX_FMT_GRAY10, AV_PIX_FMT_GRAY12, AV_PIX_FMT_GRAY14, AV_PIX_FMT_GRAY16,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUV420P9, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV422P9, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV444P9,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUV420P10, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV422P10, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV444P10,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUV420P12, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV422P12, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV444P12,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUV420P14, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV422P14, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV444P14,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_GBRP9, AV_PIX_FMT_GBRP10, AV_PIX_FMT_GBRP12, AV_PIX_FMT_GBRP14,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA444P9, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA444P10, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA444P12, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA444P16,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA422P9, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA422P10, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA422P12, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA422P16,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA420P9, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA420P10, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA420P16,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_GBRAP10,   AV_PIX_FMT_GBRAP12,    AV_PIX_FMT_GBRAP16,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_NONE
+    };
+
+    AVFilterFormats *fmts_list = ff_make_format_list(pix_fmts);
+    if (!fmts_list)
+        return AVERROR(ENOMEM);
+    return ff_set_common_formats(ctx, fmts_list);
+}
+
+static int config_output(AVFilterLink *outlink)
+{
+    AVFilterContext *ctx = outlink->src;
+    AVFilterLink *inlink = ctx->inputs[0];
+
+    outlink->time_base.num = inlink->time_base.num;
+    outlink->time_base.den = inlink->time_base.den * 2;
+    outlink->frame_rate.num = inlink->frame_rate.num * 2;
+    outlink->frame_rate.den = inlink->frame_rate.den;
+
+    return 0;
+}
+
+typedef struct ThreadData {
+    AVFrame *out, *in;
+} ThreadData;
+
+#define MIDL(type, ss)                                         \
+static unsigned midl_##ss(const type *const prev,              \
+                          const type *const next,              \
+                          int end, int x, int k)               \
+{                                                              \
+    return (prev[av_clip(x + k, 0, end)] +                     \
+            next[av_clip(x - k, 0, end)] + 1) >> 1;            \
+}
+
+MIDL(uint8_t, 8)
+MIDL(uint16_t, 16)
+
+#define MID4(type, ss)                                         \
+static unsigned mid4_##ss(const type *const prev,              \
+                          const type *const next,              \
+                          const type *const prev2,             \
+                          const type *const next2,             \
+                          int end, int x, int k, int depth)    \
+{                                                              \
+    return av_clip_uintp2_c((                                  \
+            9 * (prev[av_clip(x + k, 0, end)] +                \
+                 next[av_clip(x - k, 0, end)]) -               \
+            1 * (prev2[av_clip(x + k*3, 0, end)] +             \
+                 next2[av_clip(x - k*3, 0, end)]) + 8) >> 4,   \
+                 depth);                                       \
+}
+
+MID4(uint8_t, 8)
+MID4(uint16_t, 16)
+
+#define DIFF(type, ss)                                         \
+static unsigned diff_##ss(const type *const prev,              \
+                          const type *const next,              \
+                          int end, int x, int k, int j)        \
+{                                                              \
+    return FFABS(prev[av_clip(x + k + j, 0, end)] -            \
+                 next[av_clip(x - k + j, 0, end)]);            \
+}
+
+DIFF(uint8_t, 8)
+DIFF(uint16_t, 16)
+
+#define COST(type, ss)                                         \
+static unsigned cost_##ss(const type *const prev,              \
+                          const type *const next,              \
+                          int end, int x, int k)               \
+{                                                              \
+    const int m = midl_##ss(prev, next, end, x, k);            \
+    const int p = prev[x];                                     \
+    const int n = next[x];                                     \
+                                                               \
+    return FFABS(p - m) + FFABS(n - m);                        \
+}
+
+COST(uint8_t, 8)
+COST(uint16_t, 16)
+
+#define INTERPOLATE(type, atype, max, ss)                                      \
+static void interpolate_##ss(uint8_t *ddst,                                    \
+                             const uint8_t *const pprev_line,                  \
+                             const uint8_t *const nnext_line,                  \
+                             const uint8_t *const pprev2_line,                 \
+                             const uint8_t *const nnext2_line,                 \
+                             int x, int width, int rslope,                     \
+                             int redge, unsigned h, int depth,                 \
+                             int *K)                                           \
+{                                                                              \
+    type *dst = (type *)ddst;                                                  \
+    const type *const prev_line = (const type *const)pprev_line;               \
+    const type *const prev2_line = (const type *const)pprev2_line;             \
+    const type *const next_line = (const type *const)nnext_line;               \
+    const type *const next2_line = (const type *const)nnext2_line;             \
+    const int end = width - 1;                                                 \
+    const atype f = redge + 2;                                                 \
+    atype sd[S], sD[S], di = 0;                                                \
+    atype dmin = max;                                                          \
+    int k = *K;                                                                \
+                                                                               \
+    for (int i = -rslope; i <= rslope && abs(k) > rslope; i++) {               \
+        atype sum = 0;                                                         \
+                                                                               \
+        for (int j = -redge; j <= redge; j++) {                                \
+            sum += diff_##ss(prev_line,  next_line,  end, x, i, j);            \
+            sum += diff_##ss(prev2_line, prev_line,  end, x, i, j);            \
+            sum += diff_##ss(next_line,  next2_line, end, x, i, j);            \
+        }                                                                      \
+                                                                               \
+        sD[i + rslope]  =     sum;                                             \
+        sD[i + rslope] += f * cost_##ss(prev_line,  next_line,  end, x, i);    \
+        sD[i + rslope] += h * abs(i);                                          \
+                                                                               \
+        dmin = FFMIN(sD[i + rslope], dmin);                                    \
+    }                                                                          \
+                                                                               \
+    for (int i = -rslope; i <= rslope; i++) {                                  \
+        atype sum = 0;                                                         \
+                                                                               \
+        for (int j = -redge; j <= redge; j++) {                                \
+            sum += diff_##ss(prev_line,  next_line,  end, x, k + i, j);        \
+            sum += diff_##ss(prev2_line, prev_line,  end, x, k + i, j);        \
+            sum += diff_##ss(next_line,  next2_line, end, x, k + i, j);        \
+        }                                                                      \
+                                                                               \
+        sd[i + rslope]  =     sum;                                             \
+        sd[i + rslope] += f * cost_##ss(prev_line, next_line, end, x, k + i);  \
+        sd[i + rslope] += h * abs(k + i);                                      \
+                                                                               \
+        dmin = FFMIN(sd[i + rslope], dmin);                                    \
+    }                                                                          \
+                                                                               \
+    for (int i = -rslope; i <= rslope && abs(k) > rslope; i++) {               \
+        if (dmin == sD[i + rslope]) {                                          \
+            di = 1;                                                            \
+            k = i;                                                             \
+            break;                                                             \
+        }                                                                      \
+    }                                                                          \
+                                                                               \
+    for (int i = -rslope; i <= rslope && !di; i++) {                           \
+        if (dmin == sd[i + rslope]) {                                          \
+            k += i;                                                            \
+            break;                                                             \
+        }                                                                      \
+    }                                                                          \
+                                                                               \
+    dst[x] = mid4_##ss(prev_line, next_line, prev2_line, next2_line,           \
+                       end, x, k, depth);                                      \
+                                                                               \
+    *K = k;                                                                    \
+}
+
+INTERPOLATE(uint8_t,  unsigned, UINT_MAX, 8)
+INTERPOLATE(uint16_t, uint64_t, UINT64_MAX, 16)
+
+static int deinterlace_slice(AVFilterContext *ctx, void *arg,
+                             int jobnr, int nb_jobs)
+{
+    ESTDIFContext *s = ctx->priv;
+    ThreadData *td = arg;
+    AVFrame *out = td->out;
+    AVFrame *in = td->in;
+    const int rslope = s->rslope;
+    const int redge = s->redge;
+    const int half = s->half;
+    const int depth = s->depth;
+    const int interlaced = in->interlaced_frame;
+    const int tff = (s->field == (s->parity == -1 ? interlaced ? in->top_field_first : 1 :
+                                  s->parity ^ 1));
+
+    for (int plane = 0; plane < s->nb_planes; plane++) {
+        const uint8_t *src_data = in->data[plane];
+        uint8_t *dst_data = out->data[plane];
+        const int linesize = s->linesize[plane];
+        const int width = s->planewidth[plane];
+        const int height = s->planeheight[plane];
+        const int src_linesize = in->linesize[plane];
+        const int dst_linesize = out->linesize[plane];
+        const int start = (int)((int64_t)height * jobnr / nb_jobs);
+        const int end = (int)((int64_t)height * (jobnr + 1) / nb_jobs);
+        const uint8_t *prev_line, *prev2_line, *next_line, *next2_line, *in_line;
+        uint8_t *out_line;
+        int y_out;
+
+        y_out = start + (tff ^ (start & 1));
+
+        in_line  = src_data + (y_out * src_linesize);
+        out_line = dst_data + (y_out * dst_linesize);
+
+        while (y_out < end) {
+            memcpy(out_line, in_line, linesize);
+            y_out += 2;
+            in_line  += src_linesize * 2;
+            out_line += dst_linesize * 2;
+        }
+
+        y_out = start + ((!tff) ^ (start & 1));
+        out_line = dst_data + (y_out * dst_linesize);
+
+        for (int y = y_out; y < end; y += 2) {
+            int y_prev2_in = y - 3;
+            int y_next2_in = y + 3;
+            int y_prev_in = y - 1;
+            int y_next_in = y + 1;
+            int k;
+
+            while (y_prev2_in < 0)
+                y_prev2_in += 2;
+
+            while (y_next2_in >= height)
+                y_next2_in -= 2;
+
+            while (y_prev_in < 0)
+                y_prev_in += 2;
+
+            while (y_next_in >= height)
+                y_next_in -= 2;
+
+            prev2_line = src_data + (y_prev2_in * src_linesize);
+            next2_line = src_data + (y_next2_in * src_linesize);
+
+            prev_line = src_data + (y_prev_in * src_linesize);
+            next_line = src_data + (y_next_in * src_linesize);
+
+            k = 0;
+
+            for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) {
+                s->interpolate(out_line,
+                               prev_line, next_line,
+                               prev2_line, next2_line,
+                               x, width, rslope, redge, half, depth, &k);
+            }
+
+            out_line += 2 * dst_linesize;
+        }
+    }
+
+    return 0;
+}
+
+static int filter(AVFilterContext *ctx, int is_second, AVFrame *in)
+{
+    ESTDIFContext *s = ctx->priv;
+    AVFilterLink *outlink = ctx->outputs[0];
+    AVFrame *out;
+    ThreadData td;
+
+    out = ff_get_video_buffer(outlink, outlink->w, outlink->h);
+    if (!out)
+        return AVERROR(ENOMEM);
+    av_frame_copy_props(out, in);
+    out->interlaced_frame = 0;
+    out->pts = s->pts;
+
+    td.out = out; td.in = in;
+    ctx->internal->execute(ctx, deinterlace_slice, &td, NULL,
+                           FFMIN(s->planeheight[1] / 2, s->nb_threads));
+
+    if (s->mode)
+        s->field = !s->field;
+
+    return ff_filter_frame(outlink, out);
+}
+
+static int config_input(AVFilterLink *inlink)
+{
+    AVFilterContext *ctx = inlink->dst;
+    ESTDIFContext *s = ctx->priv;
+    const AVPixFmtDescriptor *desc = av_pix_fmt_desc_get(inlink->format);
+    int ret;
+
+    if ((ret = av_image_fill_linesizes(s->linesize, inlink->format, inlink->w)) < 0)
+        return ret;
+
+    s->planeheight[1] = s->planeheight[2] = AV_CEIL_RSHIFT(inlink->h, desc->log2_chroma_h);
+    s->planeheight[0] = s->planeheight[3] = inlink->h;
+    s->planewidth[1] = s->planewidth[2] = AV_CEIL_RSHIFT(inlink->w, desc->log2_chroma_w);
+    s->planewidth[0] = s->planewidth[3] = inlink->w;
+
+    if (inlink->h < 3) {
+        av_log(ctx, AV_LOG_ERROR, "Video of less than 3 lines is not supported\n");
+        return AVERROR(EINVAL);
+    }
+
+    s->nb_planes = av_pix_fmt_count_planes(inlink->format);
+    s->nb_threads = ff_filter_get_nb_threads(ctx);
+    s->depth = desc->comp[0].depth;
+    s->interpolate = s->depth <= 8 ? interpolate_8 : interpolate_16;
+    s->half = 1 << (s->depth - 1);
+
+    return 0;
+}
+ static int filter_frame(AVFilterLink *inlink, AVFrame *in)
+{
+    AVFilterContext *ctx = inlink->dst;
+    ESTDIFContext *s = ctx->priv;
+    int ret;
+
+    if (!s->prev) {
+        s->prev = in;
+        return 0;
+    }
+
+    if ((s->deint && !in->interlaced_frame) || ctx->is_disabled) {
+        s->prev->pts *= 2;
+        ret = ff_filter_frame(ctx->outputs[0], s->prev);
+        s->prev = in;
+        return ret;
+    }
+
+    s->pts = s->prev->pts * 2;
+    ret = filter(ctx, 0, s->prev);
+    if (ret < 0 || s->mode == 0) {
+        av_frame_free(&s->prev);
+        s->prev = in;
+        return ret;
+    }
+
+    s->pts = s->prev->pts + in->pts;
+    ret = filter(ctx, 1, s->prev);
+    av_frame_free(&s->prev);
+    s->prev = in;
+    return ret;
+}
+
+static int request_frame(AVFilterLink *link)
+{
+    AVFilterContext *ctx = link->src;
+    ESTDIFContext *s = ctx->priv;
+    int ret;
+
+    if (s->eof)
+        return AVERROR_EOF;
+
+    ret = ff_request_frame(ctx->inputs[0]);
+
+    if (ret == AVERROR_EOF && s->prev) {
+        AVFrame *next = av_frame_clone(s->prev);
+
+        if (!next)
+            return AVERROR(ENOMEM);
+
+        next->pts = s->prev->pts + av_rescale_q(1, av_inv_q(ctx->outputs[0]->frame_rate),
+                                                ctx->outputs[0]->time_base);
+        s->eof = 1;
+        ret = filter_frame(ctx->inputs[0], next);
+    } else if (ret < 0) {
+        return ret;
+    }
+
+    return ret;
+}
+
+static av_cold void uninit(AVFilterContext *ctx)
+{
+    ESTDIFContext *s = ctx->priv;
+
+    av_frame_free(&s->prev);
+}
+
+static const AVFilterPad estdif_inputs[] = {
+    {
+        .name          = "default",
+        .type          = AVMEDIA_TYPE_VIDEO,
+        .filter_frame  = filter_frame,
+        .config_props  = config_input,
+    },
+    { NULL }
+};
+
+static const AVFilterPad estdif_outputs[] = {
+    {
+        .name          = "default",
+        .type          = AVMEDIA_TYPE_VIDEO,
+        .config_props  = config_output,
+        .request_frame = request_frame,
+    },
+    { NULL }
+};
+
+AVFilter ff_vf_estdif = {
+    .name          = "estdif",
+    .description   = NULL_IF_CONFIG_SMALL("Apply Edge Slope Tracing deinterlace."),
+    .priv_size     = sizeof(ESTDIFContext),
+    .priv_class    = &estdif_class,
+    .uninit        = uninit,
+    .query_formats = query_formats,
+    .inputs        = estdif_inputs,
+    .outputs       = estdif_outputs,
+    .flags         = AVFILTER_FLAG_SUPPORT_TIMELINE_INTERNAL | AVFILTER_FLAG_SLICE_THREADS,
+    .process_command = ff_filter_process_command,
+};

 @subsection Commands
 
 This filter supports the all above options as @ref{commands}.
 
+@section estdif
+
+Deinterlace the input video ("estdif" stands for "Edge Slope
+Tracing Deinterlacing Filter").
+
+Spatial only filter that uses edge slope tracing algorithm
+to interpolate missing lines.
+It accepts the following parameters:
+
+@table @option
+@item mode
+The interlacing mode to adopt. It accepts one of the following values:
+
+@table @option
+@item frame
+Output one frame for each frame.
+@item field
+Output one frame for each field.
+@end table
+
+The default value is @code{field}.
+
+@item parity
+The picture field parity assumed for the input interlaced video. It accepts one
+of the following values:
+
+@table @option
+@item tff
+Assume the top field is first.
+@item bff
+Assume the bottom field is first.
+@item auto
+Enable automatic detection of field parity.
+@end table
+
+The default value is @code{auto}.
+If the interlacing is unknown or the decoder does not export this information,
+top field first will be assumed.
+
+@item deint
+Specify which frames to deinterlace. Accepts one of the following
+values:
+
+@table @option
+@item all
+Deinterlace all frames.
+@item interlaced
+Only deinterlace frames marked as interlaced.
+@end table
+
+The default value is @code{all}.
+
+@item rslope
+Specify the search radius for edge slope tracing. Default value is 1.
+Allowed range is from 1 to 15.
+
+@item redge
+Specify the search radius for best edge matching. Default value is 2.
+Allowed range is from 0 to 15.
+@end table
+
+@subsection Commands
+This filter supports same @ref{commands} as options.
+
 @section extractplanes
 
 Extract color channel components from input video stream into
 separate grayscale video streams.

diff --git a/doc/filters.texi b/doc/filters.texi
index 813e35c2f9..93fdd1ed44 100644
--- a/doc/filters.texi
+++ b/doc/filters.texi
@@ -11063,10 +11063,74 @@ Flags to local 3x3 coordinates maps like this:
 
 @subsection Commands
 
 This filter supports the all above options as @ref{commands}.
 
+@section estdif
+
+Deinterlace the input video ("estdif" stands for "Edge Slope
+Tracing Deinterlacing Filter").
+
+Spatial only filter that uses edge slope tracing algorithm
+to interpolate missing lines.
+It accepts the following parameters:
+
+@table @option
+@item mode
+The interlacing mode to adopt. It accepts one of the following values:
+
+@table @option
+@item frame
+Output one frame for each frame.
+@item field
+Output one frame for each field.
+@end table
+
+The default value is @code{field}.
+
+@item parity
+The picture field parity assumed for the input interlaced video. It accepts one
+of the following values:
+
+@table @option
+@item tff
+Assume the top field is first.
+@item bff
+Assume the bottom field is first.
+@item auto
+Enable automatic detection of field parity.
+@end table
+
+The default value is @code{auto}.
+If the interlacing is unknown or the decoder does not export this information,
+top field first will be assumed.
+
+@item deint
+Specify which frames to deinterlace. Accepts one of the following
+values:
+
+@table @option
+@item all
+Deinterlace all frames.
+@item interlaced
+Only deinterlace frames marked as interlaced.
+@end table
+
+The default value is @code{all}.
+
+@item rslope
+Specify the search radius for edge slope tracing. Default value is 1.
+Allowed range is from 1 to 15.
+
+@item redge
+Specify the search radius for best edge matching. Default value is 2.
+Allowed range is from 0 to 15.
+@end table
+
+@subsection Commands
+This filter supports same @ref{commands} as options.
+
 @section extractplanes
 
 Extract color channel components from input video stream into
 separate grayscale video streams.

+typedef struct ESTDIFContext {
+    const AVClass *class;
+
+    int mode;             ///< 0 is frame, 1 is field
+    int parity;           ///< frame field parity
+    int deint;            ///< which frames to deinterlace
+    int rslope;           ///< best edge slope search radius
+    int redge;            ///< best edge match search radius
+    int linesize[4];      ///< bytes of pixel data per line for each plane
+    int planewidth[4];    ///< width of each plane
+    int planeheight[4];   ///< height of each plane
+    int field;            ///< which field are we on, 0 or 1
+    int eof;
+    int depth;
+    int half;
+    int nb_planes;
+    int nb_threads;
+    int64_t pts;
+    AVFrame *prev;
+
+    void (*interpolate)(uint8_t *dst,
+                        const uint8_t *prev_line, const uint8_t *next_line,
+                        const uint8_t *prev2_line, const uint8_t *next2_line,
+                        int x, int width, int rslope, int redge, unsigned half,
+                        int depth, int *K);
+} ESTDIFContext;
+
+#define MAX_R 15
+#define S     (MAX_R * 2 + 1)
+
+#define OFFSET(x) offsetof(ESTDIFContext, x)
+#define FLAGS AV_OPT_FLAG_VIDEO_PARAM|AV_OPT_FLAG_FILTERING_PARAM|AV_OPT_FLAG_RUNTIME_PARAM
+#define CONST(name, help, val, unit) { name, help, 0, AV_OPT_TYPE_CONST, {.i64=val}, 0, 0, FLAGS, unit }
+
+static const AVOption estdif_options[] = {
+    { "mode", "specify the mode", OFFSET(mode), AV_OPT_TYPE_INT, {.i64=1}, 0, 1, FLAGS, "mode" },
+    CONST("frame", "send one frame for each frame", 0, "mode"),
+    CONST("field", "send one frame for each field", 1, "mode"),
+    { "parity", "specify the assumed picture field parity", OFFSET(parity), AV_OPT_TYPE_INT, {.i64=-1}, -1, 1, FLAGS, "parity" },
+    CONST("tff",  "assume top field first",    0, "parity"),
+    CONST("bff",  "assume bottom field first", 1, "parity"),
+    CONST("auto", "auto detect parity",       -1, "parity"),
+    { "deint",  "specify which frames to deinterlace", OFFSET(deint), AV_OPT_TYPE_INT, {.i64=0}, 0, 1, FLAGS, "deint" },
+    CONST("all",        "deinterlace all frames",                       0, "deint"),
+    CONST("interlaced", "only deinterlace frames marked as interlaced", 1, "deint"),
+    { "rslope", "specify the search radius for edge slope tracing", OFFSET(rslope), AV_OPT_TYPE_INT, {.i64=1}, 1, MAX_R, FLAGS, },
+    { "redge",  "specify the search radius for best edge matching", OFFSET(redge),  AV_OPT_TYPE_INT, {.i64=2}, 0, MAX_R, FLAGS, },
+    { NULL }
+};
+
+AVFILTER_DEFINE_CLASS(estdif);
+
+static int query_formats(AVFilterContext *ctx)
+{
+    static const enum AVPixelFormat pix_fmts[] = {
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUV410P, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV411P,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUV420P, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV422P,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUV440P, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV444P,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUVJ444P, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVJ440P,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUVJ422P, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVJ420P,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUVJ411P,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA420P, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA422P, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA444P,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_GBRP, AV_PIX_FMT_GBRAP,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_GRAY8,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_GRAY9, AV_PIX_FMT_GRAY10, AV_PIX_FMT_GRAY12, AV_PIX_FMT_GRAY14, AV_PIX_FMT_GRAY16,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUV420P9, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV422P9, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV444P9,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUV420P10, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV422P10, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV444P10,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUV420P12, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV422P12, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV444P12,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUV420P14, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV422P14, AV_PIX_FMT_YUV444P14,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_GBRP9, AV_PIX_FMT_GBRP10, AV_PIX_FMT_GBRP12, AV_PIX_FMT_GBRP14,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA444P9, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA444P10, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA444P12, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA444P16,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA422P9, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA422P10, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA422P12, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA422P16,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA420P9, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA420P10, AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA420P16,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_GBRAP10,   AV_PIX_FMT_GBRAP12,    AV_PIX_FMT_GBRAP16,
+        AV_PIX_FMT_NONE
+    };
+
+    AVFilterFormats *fmts_list = ff_make_format_list(pix_fmts);
+    if (!fmts_list)

+}
+
+static int config_output(AVFilterLink *outlink)
+{
+    AVFilterContext *ctx = outlink->src;
+    AVFilterLink *inlink = ctx->inputs[0];
+
+    outlink->time_base.num = inlink->time_base.num;
+    outlink->time_base.den = inlink->time_base.den * 2;
+    outlink->frame_rate.num = inlink->frame_rate.num * 2;
+    outlink->frame_rate.den = inlink->frame_rate.den;
+
+    return 0;
+}
+
+typedef struct ThreadData {
+    AVFrame *out, *in;
+} ThreadData;
+
+#define MIDL(type, ss)                                         \
+static unsigned midl_##ss(const type *const prev,              \
+                          const type *const next,              \
+                          int end, int x, int k)               \
+{                                                              \
+    return (prev[av_clip(x + k, 0, end)] +                     \
+            next[av_clip(x - k, 0, end)] + 1) >> 1;            \
+}
+
+MIDL(uint8_t, 8)
+MIDL(uint16_t, 16)
+
+#define MID4(type, ss)                                         \
+static unsigned mid4_##ss(const type *const prev,              \
+                          const type *const next,              \
+                          const type *const prev2,             \
+                          const type *const next2,             \
+                          int end, int x, int k, int depth)    \
+{                                                              \
+    return av_clip_uintp2_c((                                  \
+            9 * (prev[av_clip(x + k, 0, end)] +                \
+                 next[av_clip(x - k, 0, end)]) -               \
+            1 * (prev2[av_clip(x + k*3, 0, end)] +             \
+                 next2[av_clip(x - k*3, 0, end)]) + 8) >> 4,   \
+                 depth);                                       \
+}
+
+MID4(uint8_t, 8)
+MID4(uint16_t, 16)
+
+#define DIFF(type, ss)                                         \
+static unsigned diff_##ss(const type *const prev,              \
+                          const type *const next,              \
+                          int end, int x, int k, int j)        \
+{                                                              \
+    return FFABS(prev[av_clip(x + k + j, 0, end)] -            \
+                 next[av_clip(x - k + j, 0, end)]);            \
+}
+
+DIFF(uint8_t, 8)
+DIFF(uint16_t, 16)
+
+#define COST(type, ss)                                         \
+static unsigned cost_##ss(const type *const prev,              \
+                          const type *const next,              \
+                          int end, int x, int k)               \
+{                                                              \
+    const int m = midl_##ss(prev, next, end, x, k);            \
+    const int p = prev[x];                                     \
+    const int n = next[x];                                     \
+                                                               \
+    return FFABS(p - m) + FFABS(n - m);                        \
+}
+
+COST(uint8_t, 8)
+COST(uint16_t, 16)
+
+#define INTERPOLATE(type, atype, max, ss)                                      \
+static void interpolate_##ss(uint8_t *ddst,                                    \
+                             const uint8_t *const pprev_line,                  \
+                             const uint8_t *const nnext_line,                  \
+                             const uint8_t *const pprev2_line,                 \
+                             const uint8_t *const nnext2_line,                 \
+                             int x, int width, int rslope,                     \
+                             int redge, unsigned h, int depth,                 \
+                             int *K)                                           \
+{                                                                              \
+    type *dst = (type *)ddst;                                                  \
+    const type *const prev_line = (const type *const)pprev_line;               \
+    const type *const prev2_line = (const type *const)pprev2_line;             \
+    const type *const next_line = (const type *const)nnext_line;               \
+    const type *const next2_line = (const type *const)nnext2_line;             \
+    const int end = width - 1;                                                 \
+    const atype f = redge + 2;                                                 \
+    atype sd[S], sD[S], di = 0;                                                \
+    atype dmin = max;                                                          \
+    int k = *K;                                                                \
+                                                                               \
+    for (int i = -rslope; i <= rslope && abs(k) > rslope; i++) {               \
+        atype sum = 0;                                                         \
+                                                                               \
+        for (int j = -redge; j <= redge; j++) {                                \
+            sum += diff_##ss(prev_line,  next_line,  end, x, i, j);            \
+            sum += diff_##ss(prev2_line, prev_line,  end, x, i, j);            \
+            sum += diff_##ss(next_line,  next2_line, end, x, i, j);            \
+        }                                                                      \
+                                                                               \
+        sD[i + rslope]  =     sum;                                             \
+        sD[i + rslope] += f * cost_##ss(prev_line,  next_line,  end, x, i);    \
+        sD[i + rslope] += h * abs(i);                                          \
+                                                                               \
+        dmin = FFMIN(sD[i + rslope], dmin);                                    \
+    }                                                                          \
+                                                                               \
+    for (int i = -rslope; i <= rslope; i++) {                                  \
+        atype sum = 0;                                                         \
+                                                                               \
+        for (int j = -redge; j <= redge; j++) {                                \
+            sum += diff_##ss(prev_line,  next_line,  end, x, k + i, j);        \
+            sum += diff_##ss(prev2_line, prev_line,  end, x, k + i, j);        \
+            sum += diff_##ss(next_line,  next2_line, end, x, k + i, j);        \
+        }                                                                      \
+                                                                               \
+        sd[i + rslope]  =     sum;                                             \
+        sd[i + rslope] += f * cost_##ss(prev_line, next_line, end, x, k + i);  \
+        sd[i + rslope] += h * abs(k + i);                                      \
+                                                                               \
+        dmin = FFMIN(sd[i + rslope], dmin);                                    \
+    }                                                                          \
+                                                                               \
+    for (int i = -rslope; i <= rslope && abs(k) > rslope; i++) {               \
+        if (dmin == sD[i + rslope]) {                                          \
+            di = 1;                                                            \
+            k = i;                                                             \
+            break;                                                             \
+        }                                                                      \
+    }                                                                          \
+                                                                               \
+    for (int i = -rslope; i <= rslope && !di; i++) {                           \
+        if (dmin == sd[i + rslope]) {                                          \
+            k += i;                                                            \
+            break;                                                             \
+        }                                                                      \
+    }                                                                          \
+                                                                               \
+    dst[x] = mid4_##ss(prev_line, next_line, prev2_line, next2_line,           \
+                       end, x, k, depth);                                      \
+                                                                               \
+    *K = k;                                                                    \
+}
+
+INTERPOLATE(uint8_t,  unsigned, UINT_MAX, 8)
+INTERPOLATE(uint16_t, uint64_t, UINT64_MAX, 16)
+
+static int deinterlace_slice(AVFilterContext *ctx, void *arg,
+                             int jobnr, int nb_jobs)
+{
+    ESTDIFContext *s = ctx->priv;
+    ThreadData *td = arg;
+    AVFrame *out = td->out;
+    AVFrame *in = td->in;
+    const int rslope = s->rslope;
+    const int redge = s->redge;
+    const int half = s->half;
+    const int depth = s->depth;
+    const int interlaced = in->interlaced_frame;
+    const int tff = (s->field == (s->parity == -1 ? interlaced ? in->top_field_first : 1 :
+                                  s->parity ^ 1));
+
+    for (int plane = 0; plane < s->nb_planes; plane++) {
+        const uint8_t *src_data = in->data[plane];
+        uint8_t *dst_data = out->data[plane];
+        const int linesize = s->linesize[plane];
+        const int width = s->planewidth[plane];
+        const int height = s->planeheight[plane];
+        const int src_linesize = in->linesize[plane];
+        const int dst_linesize = out->linesize[plane];
+        const int start = (height * jobnr) / nb_jobs;
+        const int end = (height * (jobnr+1)) / nb_jobs;
+        const uint8_t *prev_line, *prev2_line, *next_line, *next2_line, *in_line;
+        uint8_t *out_line;
+        int y_out;
+
+        y_out = start + (tff ^ (start & 1));
+
+        in_line  = src_data + (y_out * src_linesize);
+        out_line = dst_data + (y_out * dst_linesize);
+
+        while (y_out < end) {
+            memcpy(out_line, in_line, linesize);
+            y_out += 2;
+            in_line  += src_linesize * 2;
+            out_line += dst_linesize * 2;
+        }
+
+        y_out = start + ((!tff) ^ (start & 1));
+        out_line = dst_data + (y_out * dst_linesize);
+
+        for (int y = y_out; y < end; y += 2) {
+            int y_prev2_in = y - 3;
+            int y_next2_in = y + 3;
+            int y_prev_in = y - 1;
+            int y_next_in = y + 1;
+            int k;
+
+            while (y_prev2_in < 0)
+                y_prev2_in += 2;
+
+            while (y_next2_in >= height)
+                y_next2_in -= 2;
+
+            while (y_prev_in < 0)
+                y_prev_in += 2;
+
+            while (y_next_in >= height)
+                y_next_in -= 2;
+
+            prev2_line = src_data + (y_prev2_in * src_linesize);
+            next2_line = src_data + (y_next2_in * src_linesize);
+
+            prev_line = src_data + (y_prev_in * src_linesize);
+            next_line = src_data + (y_next_in * src_linesize);
+
+            k = 0;
+
+            for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) {
+                s->interpolate(out_line,
+                               prev_line, next_line,
+                               prev2_line, next2_line,
+                               x, width, rslope, redge, half, depth, &k);
+            }
+
+            out_line += 2 * dst_linesize;
+        }
+    }
+
+    return 0;
+}
+
+static int filter(AVFilterContext *ctx, int is_second, AVFrame *in)
+{
+    ESTDIFContext *s = ctx->priv;
+    AVFilterLink *outlink = ctx->outputs[0];
+    AVFrame *out;
+    ThreadData td;
+
+    out = ff_get_video_buffer(outlink, outlink->w, outlink->h);
+    if (!out)
+        return AVERROR(ENOMEM);
+    av_frame_copy_props(out, in);
+    out->interlaced_frame = 0;
+    out->pts = s->pts;
+
+    td.out = out; td.in = in;
+    ctx->internal->execute(ctx, deinterlace_slice, &td, NULL,
+                           FFMIN(s->planeheight[1] / 2, s->nb_threads));
+
+    if (s->mode)
+        s->field = !s->field;
+
+    return ff_filter_frame(outlink, out);
+}
+
+static int config_input(AVFilterLink *inlink)
+{
+    AVFilterContext *ctx = inlink->dst;
+    ESTDIFContext *s = ctx->priv;
+    const AVPixFmtDescriptor *desc = av_pix_fmt_desc_get(inlink->format);
+    int ret;
+
+    if ((ret = av_image_fill_linesizes(s->linesize, inlink->format, inlink->w)) < 0)
+        return ret;
+
+    s->planeheight[1] = s->planeheight[2] = AV_CEIL_RSHIFT(inlink->h, desc->log2_chroma_h);
+    s->planeheight[0] = s->planeheight[3] = inlink->h;
+    s->planewidth[1] = s->planewidth[2] = AV_CEIL_RSHIFT(inlink->w, desc->log2_chroma_w);
+    s->planewidth[0] = s->planewidth[3] = inlink->w;
+
+    if (inlink->h < 3) {
+        av_log(ctx, AV_LOG_ERROR, "Video of less than 3 lines is not supported\n");
+        return AVERROR(EINVAL);
+    }
+
+    s->nb_planes = av_pix_fmt_count_planes(inlink->format);
+    s->nb_threads = ff_filter_get_nb_threads(ctx);
+    s->depth = desc->comp[0].depth;
+    s->interpolate = s->depth <= 8 ? interpolate_8 : interpolate_16;
+    s->half = 1 << (s->depth - 1);
+
+    return 0;
+}
+ static int filter_frame(AVFilterLink *inlink, AVFrame *in)
+{
+    AVFilterContext *ctx = inlink->dst;
+    ESTDIFContext *s = ctx->priv;
+    int ret;
+
+    if (!s->prev) {
+        s->prev = in;
+        return 0;
+    }
+
+    if ((s->deint && !in->interlaced_frame) || ctx->is_disabled) {
+        s->prev->pts *= 2;
+        ret = ff_filter_frame(ctx->outputs[0], s->prev);
+        s->prev = in;
+        return ret;
+    }
+
+    s->pts = s->prev->pts * 2;
+    ret = filter(ctx, 0, s->prev);
+    if (ret < 0 || s->mode == 0) {
+        av_frame_free(&s->prev);
+        s->prev = in;
+        return ret;
+    }
+
+    s->pts = s->prev->pts + in->pts;
+    ret = filter(ctx, 1, s->prev);
+    av_frame_free(&s->prev);
+    s->prev = in;
+    return ret;
+}
+
+static int request_frame(AVFilterLink *link)
+{
+    AVFilterContext *ctx = link->src;
+    ESTDIFContext *s = ctx->priv;
+    int ret;
+
+    if (s->eof)
+        return AVERROR_EOF;
+
+    ret = ff_request_frame(ctx->inputs[0]);
+
+    if (ret == AVERROR_EOF && s->prev) {
+        AVFrame *next = av_frame_clone(s->prev);
+
+        if (!next)
+            return AVERROR(ENOMEM);
+
+        next->pts = s->prev->pts + av_rescale_q(1, av_inv_q(ctx->outputs[0]->frame_rate),
+                                                ctx->outputs[0]->time_base);
+        s->eof = 1;
+        ret = filter_frame(ctx->inputs[0], next);
+    } else if (ret < 0) {
+        return ret;
+    }
+
+    return ret;
+}
+
+static av_cold void uninit(AVFilterContext *ctx)
+{
+    ESTDIFContext *s = ctx->priv;
+
+    av_frame_free(&s->prev);
+}
+
+static const AVFilterPad estdif_inputs[] = {
+    {
+        .name          = "default",
+        .type          = AVMEDIA_TYPE_VIDEO,
+        .filter_frame  = filter_frame,
+        .config_props  = config_input,
+    },
+    { NULL }
+};
+
+static const AVFilterPad estdif_outputs[] = {
+    {
+        .name          = "default",
+        .type          = AVMEDIA_TYPE_VIDEO,
+        .config_props  = config_output,
+        .request_frame = request_frame,
+    },
+    { NULL }
+};

findings.message: In deinterlace_slice(), the per-thread row range [start, end) is computed as `(height * jobnr) / nb_jobs` and `(height * (jobnr+1)) / nb_jobs`, using plain `int` arithmetic for the multiplication `height * (jobnr+1)`. Because `height`, `jobnr`, and `nb_jobs` are all `int`, the multiplication is performed in 32-bit signed arithmetic before the division. For sufficiently tall frames combined with a large number of filter threads (large jobnr/nb_jobs), the intermediate product `height * (jobnr+1)` can exceed INT_MAX, causing signed integer overflow, which is undefined behavior in C. The resulting `start`/`end` values can become incorrect (e.g., negative or wrapped), leading to out-of-bounds row indices being used to compute `in_line`/`out_line` pointers (`src_data + (y_out * src_linesize)`), which can cause out-of-bounds reads/writes.
findings.suggestion: Promote the multiplication to a 64-bit type before dividing, and cast the result back to int, so that the intermediate product cannot overflow a 32-bit signed integer even for tall frames and many threads.
findings.suggestion_code:
const int start = (int)((int64_t)height * jobnr / nb_jobs);
const int end = (int)((int64_t)height * (jobnr + 1) / nb_jobs);
findings.title: Signed integer overflow in per-thread slice boundary calculation

Vulnerability (IntegerOverflow): The ADPCM Silicon Graphics N64 decoder in libavcodec/adpcm.c computes a predictor 'delta' value by summing products of decoded sample codes and 16-bit filter coefficients that are read from (attacker-controlled) codec extradata. The multiplication of these signed int values can overflow the range of 'int', which is undefined behavior in C and was detected by UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer during fuzz testing (OSS-Fuzz). An earlier commit (0c7e0ed35b) had already changed the accumulator 'delta' to unsigned and cast the sum before division, addressing overflow in the addition, but the multiplication 'sf_codes[...] * coefs[...]' itself remained purely signed, so the intermediate product could still overflow before assignment/addition. Commit b45a6d3f76 fixes this remaining case by casting one operand of the multiplication to unsigned. Root cause: The ADPCM_N64 decoder trusts filter coefficient values loaded from codec extradata (attacker-controlled) and multiplies them with decoded sample codes using plain signed 'int' arithmetic without any range validation or use of unsigned/wider arithmetic, allowing the product to exceed INT_MAX/underflow INT_MIN, which is undefined behavior in C.

findings.message: In the ADPCM_N64 decoder's sample reconstruction loop, the predictor 'delta' accumulates a running sum from multiplying decoded sample codes (sf_codes[]) with signed filter coefficients (coefs[]) taken directly from untrusted extradata. The multiplication 'sf_codes[(i-1) - k] * coefs[(o*8) + k]' is performed entirely in 'int' (signed) arithmetic. Because coefs[] values are attacker-controlled 16-bit values sign-extended into int, and sf_codes values can also be large (n * scale, where scale can be up to 1<<15), the product of two signed ints can exceed INT_MAX/underflow INT_MIN before being added into 'delta'. Signed integer overflow is undefined behavior in C and was flagged by fuzzing (UBSan). A previous partial fix (0c7e0ed35b) changed 'delta' itself to 'unsigned' and cast the final sum before dividing, which fixed overflow in the addition/division, but left the multiplication of two signed ints unprotected, so the overflow could still occur in the multiply step itself.
findings.suggestion: Cast one of the multiplicands to unsigned before multiplying so the multiply and accumulate happen entirely in unsigned arithmetic (which has well-defined wraparound semantics in C), matching the fix applied upstream: multiply by '(unsigned)coefs[(o*8) + k]' instead of the plain signed 'coefs[(o*8) + k]'. Also ensure the accumulator 'delta' itself is declared 'unsigned' (as later fixed in 0c7e0ed35b) and that the final sum is explicitly cast to 'int' before the division by 2048.

agent_reasoning: The fix addresses an out-of-bounds read in the EXR DWA decompression path. The root cause is that dc_w/dc_h were computed with a truncating shift (xsize >> 3) instead of ceiling division, while the decode loop iterates over the full block grid including partial trailing blocks. I applied the exact same two changes as the fix commit: (1) changed dc_w/dc_h computation to round up via (x + 7) >> 3, and (2) added an avpriv_request_sample() call warning when xsize/ysize aren't multiples of 8, placed at the equivalent logical point in this codebase's version of dwa_uncompress (after the compressed_size bounds check, before bytestream2_init is called to start parsing the compressed streams). The surrounding code in this snapshot lacks some checks present in later ffmpeg versions (e.g., ac_size<=0, rle_raw_size>INT_MAX), but those are unrelated to this fix and were not part of the required change, so I left them alone to keep the diff minimal and scoped to the actual vulnerability fix.

findings.message: In dwa_uncompress(), dc_w and dc_h (the number of 8x8 DC-coefficient blocks per row/column) are computed as td->xsize >> 3 and td->ysize >> 3. This integer division truncates (floors) instead of rounding up. When td->xsize or td->ysize is not a multiple of 8 (odd/non-block-aligned tile or scanline dimensions), the computed dc_w/dc_h is smaller than the actual number of 8x8 blocks that the main decode loop iterates over (for (y = 0; y < td->ysize; y += 8) / for (x = 0; x < td->xsize; x += 8)). The per-block DC index is later computed as `idx = (x >> 3) + (y >> 3) * dc_w + dc_w * dc_h * j;` and used to index into td->dc_data (cast to uint16_t*), which was allocated/populated based on dc_count derived from the bitstream, not from this truncated dc_w*dc_h product. Because dc_w*dc_h is smaller than the number of blocks actually visited, `idx` can run past the number of valid decoded DC values into unrelated/unallocated memory, or otherwise access memory that does not correspond to a real DC coefficient. This results in an out-of-bounds read (as identified by Google Big Sleep, BIGSLEEP-445392027-crash.exr) when decoding a maliciously crafted or malformed EXR file compressed with DWA and non-block-aligned tile/scanline dimensions.
findings.suggestion: Round dc_w and dc_h up to account for partial trailing 8x8 blocks, matching the block-iteration stride used later in the function, e.g. `(td->xsize + 7) >> 3` and `(td->ysize + 7) >> 3`. Additionally, since it is unclear whether the format even supports non-multiple-of-8 dimensions for DWA-compressed data, emit a sample request (avpriv_request_sample) when xsize/ysize are not multiples of 8 so real-world behavior can be verified.
findings.title: Truncated dc_w/dc_h computation causes out-of-bounds read of DC coefficient array in EXR DWA decompression

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Truncated dc_w/dc_h computation causes out-of-bounds read of DC coefficient array in EXR DWA decompression

ground_truth.root_cause: Use of truncating integer division (>> 3, i.e. floor(x/8)) to compute the number of 8x8 blocks per dimension, instead of ceiling division, when the corresponding pixel dimension is not guaranteed to be a multiple of 8. The decode loop that walks over blocks uses ceiling-like iteration (steps of 8 covering the full xsize/ysize including a partial last block), creating an inconsistency between the computed grid size (dc_w * dc_h) and the actual number of blocks processed.

Vulnerability (BufferOverflow): The ProRes RAW decoder (libavcodec/prores_raw.c), added in commit 589b3ed943, computed the 16-byte-aligned coded_width/coded_height for the decoded frame before calling ff_set_dimensions() to update avctx->width/height when the stream's resolution changes. ff_set_dimensions() internally also sets avctx->coded_width/coded_height (to the unaligned width/height), so calling it after the manual alignment assignment caused the aligned values to be discarded/overwritten with unaligned ones. This was found via OSS-Fuzz (case 438771336) and fixed in c9e93df4eed93fe0044c52d953688c4180de1d48 by simply reordering the two code blocks so the alignment assignment happens after ff_set_dimensions(). Root cause: Incorrect ordering of two dimension-setting operations: the aligned coded_width/coded_height assignment happened before a call to ff_set_dimensions(), which itself also assigns (unaligned) values to those same fields, silently overwriting the alignment performed just before it.

findings.message: In decode_frame() of the newly added ProRes RAW decoder, avctx->coded_width and avctx->coded_height are set to the 16-byte aligned values of the parsed frame width/height BEFORE the call to ff_set_dimensions(avctx, w, h). ff_set_dimensions() internally resets avctx->coded_width and avctx->coded_height back to the unaligned width/height (w, h) whenever the resolution changes from the previous frame. As a result, the carefully computed aligned coded dimensions are silently clobbered with the unaligned values. Later frame-buffer allocation and pixel-writing code in this decoder assumes the frame buffer was allocated using the 16-aligned coded_width/coded_height, so when w or h is not a multiple of 16, the actual allocated/output buffer is smaller than what the decoder writes into, producing a heap buffer overflow (found by OSS-Fuzz, case 438771336). This can be triggered simply by feeding a ProRes RAW stream whose resolution changes to a non-16-aligned width/height between frames.
findings.suggestion: Move the assignment of avctx->coded_width/coded_height (using FFALIGN) to AFTER the call to ff_set_dimensions(), so the aligned coded dimensions are not overwritten by ff_set_dimensions()'s own (unaligned) coded_width/coded_height assignment.

agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix e90c2ff4b5a5 on top of intro fe1ffd63fb09 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (OutOfBoundsRead): parse_itut_t35_metadata() in libavcodec/libdav1d.c parses ITU-T T.35 metadata OBUs emitted by the dav1d AV1 decoder. For payloads whose country_code identifies the United States (ITU_T_T35_COUNTRY_CODE_US, 0xB5), the function reads a 16-bit provider_code from the payload buffer using bytestream2_get_be16u(), the unchecked variant of the bytestream2 API that performs no bounds checking against the remaining buffer length. If an attacker supplies a crafted AV1 bitstream containing an ITU-T T.35 metadata OBU with country_code = 0xB5 and a payload shorter than 2 bytes (e.g. 1 byte), the unchecked read walks past the end of the allocated payload buffer, triggering a heap-buffer-overflow read of up to 2 bytes as confirmed by AddressSanitizer. Root cause: During a refactor that converted the country_code/provider_code dispatch logic in parse_itut_t35_metadata() into nested switch statements, the previously bounds-checked bytestream2_get_be16() call used to read provider_code was replaced by the unchecked bytestream2_get_be16u() variant for the US country_code case, without adding an explicit length check (bytestream2_get_bytes_left(&gb) < 2) beforehand. The analogous branch for the UK country code does include such a guard, but it was inconsistently omitted for the US branch, leaving a gap where attacker-controlled short payloads are read out of bounds.

avcodec/libdav1d: fix heap overflow in US ITU-T T.35 metadata parsing

The US country_code path in parse_itut_t35_metadata() reads the
the provider_code with bytestream2_get_be16u(), which is a
unchecked version that does not validate the remaining
length before reading. When an AV1 stream contains ITU-T T.35
metadata with country_code set to 0xB5 (which is US) and a
payload shorter than 2 bytes, this results in a heap overflow
reading 2 bytes past the allocation.

The UK country code already guards against this issue by
checking it before the unchecked read. We're using the same
pattern to the US country code path.

Pwno crafted an AV1 IVF with a metadata OBU containing ITU-T T.35
with country_code=0xB5 and a 1-byte payload. Decoding with libdav1d
triggers the overflow. ASan says:

  #1 bytestream2_get_be16u src/libavcodec/bytestream.h:98
  #2 parse_itut_t35_metadata src/libavcodec/libdav1d.c:376

findings.message: In parse_itut_t35_metadata(), when refactoring the country_code/provider_code dispatch into a switch statement, the read of provider_code for the US (ITU_T_T35_COUNTRY_CODE_US) branch was changed from the bounds-checked bytestream2_get_be16() to the unchecked bytestream2_get_be16u() variant, with no prior validation that at least 2 bytes remain in the GetByteContext (gb). bytestream2_get_be16u() (see libavcodec/bytestream.h) does not verify bytestream2_get_bytes_left(&gb) before reading, so if the ITU-T T.35 payload has country_code == 0xB5 (US) and a payload shorter than 2 bytes (e.g. 1 byte), the read overruns the end of the payload buffer by up to 2 bytes, producing a heap-buffer-overflow read. The analogous UK country_code path elsewhere in the function already guards this with an explicit bytestream2_get_bytes_left() check before the unchecked read, but the equivalent guard was omitted for the US path in this refactor.
findings.suggestion: Validate the remaining bytes in the GetByteContext before performing the unchecked 16-bit read, matching the pattern already used for the UK country_code branch: check bytestream2_get_bytes_left(&gb) < 2 and return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA (or otherwise bail out) before calling bytestream2_get_be16u(). Alternatively, use the bounds-checked bytestream2_get_be16() variant instead of the 'u' (unchecked) variant.

This way the encoder does not need to access the decoder AVCodecContext,

findings.message: In dec_open(), the newly introduced Decoder.subtitle_header field is assigned directly from ist->dec_ctx->subtitle_header (a pointer owned/managed by the decoder's AVCodecContext, i.e. by libavcodec). No copy of the underlying buffer is made; Decoder.subtitle_header is simply an alias to memory owned by the AVCodecContext. When the AVCodecContext is later closed/freed (avcodec_free_context, e.g. during decoder teardown or dec_free), the buffer that subtitle_header points to can be released or reallocated by libavcodec, while consumers of Decoder.subtitle_header (e.g. the subtitle encoder path which reads dec->subtitle_header/subtitle_header_size to initialize its own codec context) may still read from it afterward, resulting in a use-after-free / dangling pointer read. The field was also declared as `const uint8_t *`, further indicating the intent was only to reference, not own, the memory, with no corresponding free path.
findings.suggestion: Deep-copy the subtitle_header buffer into memory owned by the Decoder struct instead of storing a raw pointer into the AVCodecContext. Allocate a buffer of subtitle_header_size (+1 for NUL termination, since ASS code assumes a null-terminated buffer), memcpy the contents, and free it explicitly when the Decoder is destroyed (dec_free). Change the field type from `const uint8_t *` to a mutable, decoder-owned `uint8_t *` so ownership is clear.
findings.title: Decoder.subtitle_header stores a borrowed pointer into the AVCodecContext, leading to use-after-free

agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 770bc1c23a18 on top of intro baad75cafa6b via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (BufferOverflow): libavcodec/aac/aacdec_usac_mps212.c implements MPEG Surround (Mpsp212) lossless-data decoding for USAC AAC streams. The function ff_aac_ec_data_dec() calls get_freq_strides(), which computes per-band stride boundaries and writes data_bands+1 entries into the caller-supplied output array. The function was called with ld->freq_res (a 9-entry, per-parameter-set array) as that output buffer instead of a dedicated scratch buffer sized for the number of frequency bands (up to 28+1). Because data_bands is derived from start_band/end_band/band_stride and can exceed MPS_MAX_PARAM_SETS, this results in an out-of-bounds write into the AACMPSLosslessData structure, and the corrupted/overflowed values are then read back and used as array indices into ld->last_data, causing further out-of-bounds accesses. An intermediate fix (c2364e92) attempted to mitigate this by clamping the written values to 2 bits, but that only reduced (did not eliminate) the aliasing/overflow problem and was itself reverted; the real fix (770bc1c23a) introduces a properly sized local temporary array (freq_stride_map) so get_freq_strides() no longer writes into ld->freq_res at all. Root cause: The output buffer passed to get_freq_strides() (ld->freq_res, sized for MPS_MAX_PARAM_SETS=9 per-set entries) is too small for the number of entries the function actually writes (up to data_bands+1, where data_bands can reach 28 for the finest stride/widest band range). Additionally, using ld->freq_res as both an input (ld->freq_res[set_idx] selects band_stride) and output (overwritten in-place with band-index data) creates unintended aliasing that corrupts state used later in the same function.

findings.message: In ff_aac_ec_data_dec(), get_freq_strides() is called with ld->freq_res used directly as the output ('freq_strides') scratch buffer: `get_freq_strides(ld->freq_res, stride_table[ld->freq_res[set_idx]], start_band, end_band)`. ld->freq_res is declared as `int16_t freq_res[MPS_MAX_PARAM_SETS]` (MPS_MAX_PARAM_SETS == 9), i.e. it is meant to hold one frequency-resolution value per parameter set. However get_freq_strides() writes indices 0..data_bands inclusive into this buffer, where data_bands = (end_band - start_band - 1) / band_stride + 1. Since band_stride can be as small as 1 (stride_table[0] == 1) and end_band can be as large as MPS_MAX_PARAM_BANDS (28), data_bands can be up to 28, so get_freq_strides() can write up to 29 int16_t entries into a 9-element array, producing a large out-of-bounds write that corrupts adjacent fields of the AACMPSLosslessData structure (coarse_quant_no, etc.) and its own control data (ld->freq_res[set_idx]) that is still being read in the same function. The subsequent reads `ld->last_data[ld->freq_res[j]]` and `ld->freq_res[j + 0]`/`ld->freq_res[j + 1]` used as array indices into ld->last_data (size MPS_MAX_PARAM_BANDS) then use corrupted/attacker-influenced values, leading to further out-of-bounds reads/writes on ld->last_data. This is triggerable via a crafted USAC/MPEG-Surround (Mpsp212) AAC bitstream.
findings.suggestion: Do not reuse ld->freq_res (a MPS_MAX_PARAM_SETS-sized, per-parameter-set array) as the scratch buffer that get_freq_strides() fills with per-band stride boundaries. Use a local temporary array sized for the maximum number of frequency bands (e.g. int16_t freq_stride_map[MPS_MAX_PARAM_BANDS + 1]) as the destination for get_freq_strides(), and use that temporary array for all subsequent indexing (ld->last_data[freq_stride_map[j]], freq_stride_map[j+0]..freq_stride_map[j+1]) instead of ld->freq_res. This avoids aliasing/overwriting the control array and avoids out-of-bounds writes since data_bands can exceed MPS_MAX_PARAM_SETS.
findings.title: Out-of-bounds write on ld->freq_res via get_freq_strides() aliasing in ff_aac_ec_data_dec()

ground_truth.root_cause: The output buffer passed to get_freq_strides() (ld->freq_res, sized for MPS_MAX_PARAM_SETS=9 per-set entries) is too small for the number of entries the function actually writes (up to data_bands+1, where data_bands can reach 28 for the finest stride/widest band range). Additionally, using ld->freq_res as both an input (ld->freq_res[set_idx] selects band_stride) and output (overwritten in-place with band-index data) creates unintended aliasing that corrupts state used later in the same function.

agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 2e32276872d3 on top of intro baad75cafa6b via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (BufferOverflow): The USAC MPS212 (MPEG Surround) entropy-coded pair decoder ec_pair_dec() in libavcodec/aac/aacdec_usac_mps212.c passes a local pointer array p_data[2] into huff_decode(), which for certain bitstream configurations (2D time-differential coding with diff_freq set) advances the pointers by one element as a side effect (data[0] += 1; data[1] += 1;). Since the pointer array is passed by reference, this advancement is visible to the caller. The caller then reuses these now-advanced pointers, still bounded by the full nb_bands count, as both source and destination for attach_lsb(), which walks nb_bands elements starting at the (possibly advanced) pointer. This can read and write one int16_t element past the end of the fixed-size 28-element stack arrays that back the pointers, corrupting adjacent stack memory. Root cause: huff_decode() mutates the caller's array-of-pointers argument (advancing data[0]/data[1] by one element in certain code paths) as an implementation detail to signal 'first element already consumed', but ec_pair_dec() was written assuming p_data[] always points at the base of the fixed-size data_pair[] arrays. Combined with an unconditional fixed iteration count (nb_bands) in attach_lsb(), the mismatch between the (possibly shifted) pointer and the full-length loop bound produces an out-of-bounds access.

Combined with an unconditional fixed iteration count (nb_bands) in attach_lsb(), the mismatch between the (possibly shifted) pointer and the full-length loop bound produces an out-of-bounds access.

agent_reasoning: The intro commit added MPS212 bitstream parsing but did not validate the attacker-controlled bsOttBandsPhase and bsResidualBands fields against the legal number of bands (numBands) derived from bsFreqRes. These fields are later used as loop/array bounds in parse_mps212(), enabling an out-of-bounds read for crafted files. I applied the same fix as fix_sha: reject bsFreqRes==0, compute numBands via the Table 39 lookup, validate both fields against numBands (returning AVERROR_INVALIDDATA on violation), and use the Table 109 default for otts_bands_phase when not explicitly present. The resulting diff matches the fix commit's diff exactly and applies cleanly against intro_parent.

findings.message: decode_usac_element_pair() reads the raw 5-bit bitstream fields bsOttBandsPhase (via get_bits(gb, 5)) into e->mps.otts_bands_phase, and, when residual coding is enabled, bsResidualBands into e->mps.residual_bands, without validating them against the maximum number of frequency bands (numBands) allowed for the current freq_res setting (per ISO/IEC 23003-1:2007 Table 39, numBands can be as small as 4). Because e->mps.otts_bands_phase is left unbounded (0-31 from 5 bits) it is later used directly as the 'nb_bands' argument passed into ff_aac_ec_data_dec()/parse_mps212() when decoding the OTT IPD (Inter-channel Phase Difference) data, and e->mps.residual_bands is also left unbounded and later combined via FFMAX with otts_bands_phase. Since these values control loop bounds/array indices used to fill fixed-size per-band arrays inside the MPEG Surround (MPS212) decoding path (parse_mps212 / ff_aac_ec_data_dec / ff_aac_map_index_data), a malicious bitstream can supply an out-of-range value larger than the actual number of bands, causing writes/reads beyond the allocated per-band buffers -- an out-of-bounds array access as confirmed by the reporter's PoC (matejsmycka/poc.mp4).
findings.suggestion: Compute the maximum permitted number of bands (numBands) for the given freq_res (per ISO/IEC 23003-1:2007 Table 39) and validate that both bsOttBandsPhase and bsResidualBands do not exceed it, returning AVERROR_INVALIDDATA otherwise, before the values are used to size/index per-band arrays later in parse_mps212(). This is exactly what the fix commit ddcb9dd3b5d21d055774abd61ae609ecb728cb1c implements.
findings.title: Missing range validation of bsOttBandsPhase/bsResidualBands allows out-of-bounds array access in MPS212 (parametric stereo) decoding

agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix f435ce22e10e on top of intro 6d0c89980c78 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (UseAfterFree): In libavcodec/h2645_sei.c, the function h2645_sei_to_side_data() handles conversion of parsed HEVC/H.264 SEI messages (including Ambient Viewing Environment) into AVFrameSideData. For the Ambient Viewing Environment SEI, code allocates an AVAmbientViewingEnvironment struct, wraps it in an AVBufferRef, and calls ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext() to attach it as frame side data, transferring ownership of the buffer. Only after this call does the code populate the struct's ambient_illuminance/ambient_light_x/ambient_light_y fields. Because ownership of the underlying buffer can already be transferred or the buffer already released as part of that call's internal handling (in success or error paths), writing to dst_env afterwards can operate on memory that could already have been freed/exposed elsewhere, producing a use-after-free. This was found via fuzzing with a crafted MP4/HVCC sample (poc_hvcc_modified.mp4). Root cause: The struct fields for the newly-allocated side-data object are initialized AFTER handing the wrapping buffer off to a function (ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext) that can take ownership of / free that buffer, instead of before. This creates a window in which the memory the code is about to write to is no longer guaranteed to be valid/owned by this code path.

findings.message: In h2645_sei_to_side_data(), when handling the Ambient Viewing Environment SEI, a new AVAmbientViewingEnvironment struct (dst_env) is allocated and wrapped in an AVBufferRef (buf), which is then handed off to ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext(). This function can fail (returning ret < 0) after having already taken ownership of / freed the buffer (e.g. if av_frame_side_data_add fails or another internal error occurs, the buffer ref is unreferenced/freed as part of cleanup). The code checks 'if (ret < 0) return ret;' correctly to bail out in that case, but only AFTER the buffer has potentially been consumed/freed. However, the fields dst_env->ambient_illuminance, dst_env->ambient_light_x, and dst_env->ambient_light_y are written AFTER the call to ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext succeeds check, but that write itself happens on the object that could have been freed as part of a partial failure inside ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext before it returns an error code being checked; more critically, on the success path the ownership of dst_env's underlying buffer has already been transferred to the side-data list, but the fields are still populated afterwards, i.e. dst_env may already be exposed to other consumers (e.g. other threads via frame side data, or freed if the ext function internally frees the buffer on certain failure paths) before initialization completes. This ordering was flagged by fuzzing (poc_hvcc_modified.mp4) as leading to a use-after-free: the buffer can be deallocated before its listed fields are initialized, because the struct data is only initialized after the call that can transfer/release ownership of the buffer, rather than before it.
findings.suggestion: Initialize dst_env->ambient_illuminance, ambient_light_x, and ambient_light_y BEFORE calling ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext(), so that the AVAmbientViewingEnvironment struct is fully populated before ownership of its backing buffer can be transferred or released by that call. This matches the actual upstream fix which moves the three assignment lines to occur immediately after allocation/before the side-data-adding call that may free/transfer the buffer on error or success paths.
findings.title: Use-after-free: AmbientViewingEnvironment side data written after side-data buffer may be freed on error path

agent_reasoning: The fix commit replaces the manual single-reflection boundary mirroring in vif_filter1d (vertical and horizontal passes) with avpriv_mirror(), which correctly handles arbitrarily large overshoot by repeatedly folding the index back into range. In the target codebase, "internal.h" (relative include, matching this snapshot's include style) already provides avpriv_mirror via libavutil/internal.h, so no new include was needed — only the two index computations were changed to call avpriv_mirror(ii, h - 1) and avpriv_mirror(jj, w - 1) respectively, matching the fix commit's semantic change exactly.
commit_message:
avfilter: add vif filter

fix_commit_message:
avfilter/vf_vif: Fix out of array access with small dimensions

The hand written boundary mirroring reflected an out of range index only
once, which is insufficient when the image dimension is smaller than the
filter half width (filt_w/2 == 8). A 1x1 input made the index reach 8
and -7, reading out of the src[]/temp[] arrays. Use avpriv_mirror(),
which mirrors repeatedly and stays in range for any dimension.

findings.message: In vif_filter1d(), when computing the vertical and horizontal 1D filter passes near image edges, out-of-range indices ii/jj are 'mirrored' back into range using a single-step reflection: `ii = ii < 0 ? -ii : (ii >= h ? 2*h - ii - 1 : ii)` (and analogously for jj/w). This single reflection only corrects an index that is out of range by up to h (or w) once. Because the filter half-width is filt_w/2 == 8, an index can be out of range by more than the image dimension when h or w is smaller than filt_w/2 (e.g. a 1x1 input). In that case a single reflection does not bring the index back into [0, h-1] (or [0, w-1]); the resulting ii/jj can still be negative or >= h/w (e.g. reaching 8 or -7 for h=w=1), causing src[ii*src_stride+j] and temp[jj] to be read out of bounds, leading to an out-of-bounds heap read / undefined behavior.
findings.suggestion: Replace the hand-rolled single-step reflection with a proper repeated mirroring function such as FFmpeg's avpriv_mirror(), which repeatedly folds the index back into range and is correct regardless of how small the dimension is relative to the filter width. E.g. `ii = avpriv_mirror(ii, h - 1);` and `jj = avpriv_mirror(jj, w - 1);`. Include libavutil/internal.h for avpriv_mirror().
findings.title: Insufficient boundary mirroring causes out-of-bounds array access with small image dimensions

ground_truth.root_cause: The mirroring/reflection logic used to clamp filter indices near image boundaries was implemented as a single conditional reflection (`ii < 0 ? -ii : ...`) rather than a proper repeated/folded mirroring, which is only valid when the amount of overshoot does not exceed the array dimension itself. Small image dimensions (smaller than filt_w/2) violate this assumption, allowing indices computed as `i - filt_w/2 + filt_i` to overshoot by more than h or w, producing indices still out of the valid [0, dim-1] range after one reflection.

agent_reasoning: The bug was a stack buffer overflow: `float en[2]` was only 2 elements, but the direction loop `for (g = 0; g < tns->n_filt[w]; g++)` could iterate with g=0,1,2 when n_filt=3 (AAC Main profile, long windows, order==TNS_MAX_ORDER). The access `en[g]` with g=2 reads past the end of the array. Additionally, `en[!g]` (logical NOT) evaluates to en[0] for g>=1, which was semantically wrong for g=1 and caused an out-of-bounds read for g=2. The fix expands `en` to 4 elements, measures energy across 3 frequency segments for the 3-filter case, and corrects the direction comparison to `en[g] < en[g+1]`, ensuring all accesses stay within bounds and the comparison is semantically correct for each filter.
commit_message:
[Merged] aacenc_tns: tune and reduce artifacts

There are a couple of major changes here:

1. Start using TNS coefficient compression.
2. Start using 3 bits per coefficient maximum for short windows.
The bits we save from these 2 changes seem to make a nice impact on the
rest of the file/windows.

3. Remove special case gain checking for short windows.
4. Modify the coefficient loop to support up to 3 windows.
The additional restrictions on TNS were something that was no in the
specifications and furthermore restricting TNS to only low energy short
windows was done to compensate for bugs elsewhere in the code.

Overall, the improvements here reduce crackling artifacts heard in very
noisy tracks.

Signed-off-by: Rostislav Pehlivanov <atomnuker@gmail.com>
fix_commit_message:
aacenc_tns: clamp filter direction energy measurement

The issue is that:

float en[2];
...
tns->n_filt[w] = is8 ? 1 : order != TNS_MAX_ORDER ? 2 : 3;
for (g = 0; g < tns->n_filt[w]; g++) {
    tns->direction[w][g] = slant != 2 ? slant : en[g] < en[!g];

When using the AAC Main profile, n_filt = 3, and slant is by
default 2 (normal long frames), g can go above 1.

en is the evolution of energy in the frequency domain for every
band at the given window. E.g. whether the energy is concentrated
at the top of each band, or the bottom.

For 2-pole filters, its straightforward.
For 3-pole filters, we need more than 2 measurements.

This commit properly implements support for 3-pole filters, by measuring
the band energy across three areas.

Do note that even xHE-AAC caps n_filt to 2, and only AAC Main allows
n_filt == 3.

Fixes https://trac.ffmpeg.org/ticket/11418

aacenc_tns: tune and reduce artifacts

2. Start using 3 bits per coefficient maximum for short windows.
The bits we save from these 2 changes seem to make a nice impact on the
rest of the file/windows.

3. Remove special case gain checking for short windows.
4. Modify the coefficient loop to support up to 3 windows.
The additional restrictions on TNS were something that was no in the
specifications and furthermore restricting TNS to only low energy short
windows was done to compensate for bugs elsewhere in the code.

Overall, the improvements here reduce crackling artifacts heard in very

Signed-off-by: Rostislav Pehlivanov <atomnuker@gmail.com>
pr_description:
The TNS filter direction is determined by comparing energy levels across different frequency regions. Previously, energy was only measured in two segments (start and end), which worked correctly for 1- or 2-filter configurations. However, when using AAC Main profile with long windows, `n_filt` can be 3, requiring energy comparisons across three regions for each filter's direction decision.

This commit renames `n_filt` to a pre-computed constant (shared across all windows, since it only depends on window type and order), expands the energy array from 2 to 4 elements, and adds proper 3-segment energy measurement when `n_filt != 2`. For the 2-filter case, the band energy is split into start and end halves as before, with `en[2] = en[0]` to support the symmetric direction comparison. For the 1- or 3-filter case, the band energy is measured in three thirds (start, middle, end), with `en[3] = en[0]` for the wraparound comparison.

The filter direction comparison is updated from `en[g] < en[!g]` to `en[g] < en[g + 1]`, which correctly expresses "is the energy in this band's region lower than the next region" for all filter indices including g=2 in the 3-filter case.
pr_title: aacenc_tns: properly support 3-filter TNS direction energy measurement

findings.message: The array `en` is declared as `float en[2]` (2 elements, indices 0 and 1), but the loop `for (g = 0; g < tns->n_filt[w]; g++)` can iterate with g=0, 1, 2 when `n_filt[w]` is set to 3 (which happens when `!is8 && order == TNS_MAX_ORDER`, i.e., AAC Main profile with long windows). Inside the loop, the expression `en[g] < en[!g]` accesses `en[2]` when g=2, which is a stack-buffer-overflow read past the end of the 2-element array. The `!g` expression also only ever evaluates to 0 or 1, so the comparison is semantically wrong for g=2 as well. An attacker can trigger this by encoding audio with the AAC Main profile (`-profile:a aac_main` or `-aac_pred true`).
findings.suggestion: Expand the `en` array to accommodate 3-filter cases (e.g., `float en[4]`) and compute energy measurements across three regions instead of two. Also change `en[g] < en[!g]` to `en[g] < en[g + 1]` so the direction comparison is meaningful for all filter indices.

Vulnerability (LogicError): When demuxing-specific fields (parse_queue, raw_packet_buffer, raw_packet_buffer_size) were moved from FFFormatContext to FormatContextInternal, the call to ff_flush_packet_queue() in avformat_free_context() was guarded with 'if (s->iformat)' to prevent accessing demuxer-only fields on muxer contexts. However, ff_flush_packet_queue() also frees si->packet_buffer, which resides on FFFormatContext and is used by muxers (in mux.c via ff_interleave_add_packet). By guarding the entire ff_flush_packet_queue() call behind s->iformat, the muxer's packet_buffer is never freed when the format context is destroyed. If a muxing process fails while packets remain in the interleaving queue, those packets will leak. Root cause: The commit cb80ec0b moved parse_queue, raw_packet_buffer, and raw_packet_buffer_size to FormatContextInternal (demuxer-only). To prevent invalid memory access on muxer contexts, the entire ff_flush_packet_queue() call was guarded behind 'if (s->iformat)'. However, ff_flush_packet_queue() also clears si->packet_buffer which lives on FFFormatContext (accessible for both muxers and demuxers). The overly broad guard prevents packet_buffer from being freed for muxers.

agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix e262411f329d on top of intro e424abc3a093 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (NullPointerDereference): The check `if (!eval->exprs)` on line 116 only validates against a NULL pointer, but does not catch the case where `eval->exprs` is a non-NULL empty string (""). Then `av_strtok("", "|", &buf)` on line 149 returns NULL immediately since there are no tokens, so the while loop never executes and `last_expr` remains uninitialized/NULL with `nb_channels` staying at 0. Inside `av_expr_parse`, `strlen()` is called on this NULL pointer, causing a SEGV (null pointer dereference). Root cause: The input validation check `if (!eval->exprs)` only tests for a NULL pointer but not for an empty string. In C, an empty string `""` is a valid non-NULL pointer, so the check passes. @@ -428,20 +428,84 @@ A longer delay will sound like an open air concert in the mountains:
 aecho=0.8:0.9:1000:0.3
 @end example
 
 @item
 Same as above but with one more mountain:
 @example
 aecho=0.8:0.9:1000|1800:0.3|0.25
 @end example
 @end itemize
 
+@section aeval
+
+Modify an audio signal according to the specified expressions.
+
+This filter accepts one or more expressions (one for each channel),
+which are evaluated and used to modify a corresponding audio signal.
+
+This filter accepts the following options:
+
+@table @option
+@item exprs
+Set the '|'-separated expressions list for each separate channel. If
+the number of input channels is greater than the number of
+expressions, the last specified expression is used for the remaining
+output channels.
+
+@item channel_layout, c
+Set output channel layout. If not specified, the channel layout is
+specified by the number of expressions. If set to @samp{same}, it will
+use by default the same input channel layout.
+@end table
+
+Each expression in @var{exprs} can contain the following constants and functions:
+
+@table @option
+@item ch
+channel number of the current expression
+
+@item n
+number of the evaluated sample, starting from 0
+
+@item s
+sample rate
+
+@item t
+time of the evaluated sample expressed in seconds
+
+@item nb_in_channels
+@item nb_out_channels
+input and output number of channels
+
+@item val(CH)
+the value of input channel with number @var{CH}
+@end table
+
+Note: this filter is slow. For faster processing you should use a
+dedicated filter.
+
+@subsection Examples
+
+@itemize
+@item
+Half volume:
+@example
+aeval=val(ch)/2:c=same
+@end example
+
+@item
+Invert phase of the second channel:
+@example
+eval=val(0)|-val(1)
+@end example
+@end itemize
+
 @section afade
 
 Apply fade-in/out effect to input audio.
 
 A description of the accepted parameters follows.
 
 @table @option
 @item type, t
 Specify the effect type, can be either @code{in} for fade-in, or
 @code{out} for a fade-out effect. Default is @code{in}.
